mainTopic: Witnesses and women in the laws of damages, and whether half-damage (פלגא נזקא) is compensation or a fine
overview: The גמרא first explains two phrases in the משנה about who may be a witness: 'בני חורין' excludes עבדים and 'בני ברית' excludes גוים, and both phrases are needed. Next it brings three פסוקים showing that a woman is equal to a man in punishments, in civil laws, and in killings, and it explains why each פסוק is needed. Then it turns to the משנה's phrase that the ניזק and the מזיק both share in the payment. רב פפא says the half payment for a תם ox (פלגא נזקא) is ממונא, real compensation. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says it is קנסא, a fine, and the גמרא explains the reasoning behind each view. The משנה's phrase seems to fit only ממונא, but the גמרא answers that it refers to פחת נבילה. It then explains why פחת נבילה is taught twice, once for a תם and once for a מועד. Finally, a challenge from the list of differences between a תם and a מועד is defended with 'תנא ושייר', but that defense falls, and a new proof begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining 'free men' and 'members of the covenant'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two phrases from the משנה and explains that 'בני חורין' excludes עבדים and 'בני ברית' excludes גוים as witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Free men and members of the covenant.' 'Free men' comes to exclude slaves. 'Members of the covenant' comes to exclude gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from the משנה about who can testify, and explains what each phrase leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is read as an exclusion. 'בני חורין' rules out a Canaanite עבד, and 'בני ברית' rules out a גוי. This sets up the next question: why does the משנה need to say both?

phrases.english: "Free men and members of the covenant."
"Free men": to exclude slaves,
"Members of the covenant": to exclude gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section by explaining the משנה's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עבדים and גוים are excluded from testifying, each through its own phrase.

steps.title: Why both exclusions are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we could not learn the גוי from the עבד, or the עבד from the גוי, because each has a reason to be disqualified that the other lacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If we were told only about a slave, we would say it is because he has no lineage. But a gentile, who has lineage, I might say is not excluded. And if we were told only about a gentile, we would say it is because he has no connection to מצוות. But a slave, who is connected to מצוות, I might say is not excluded. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה had to mention both the עבד and the גוי, because neither case can be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד has no חייס (legal family lineage), which a גוי does have. A גוי has no connection to מצוות, while an עבד is obligated in some מצוות. Since each one has its own weakness, you could not learn one from the other, so both had to be written.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state both cases)

steps.whatToRemember: An עבד is weak in lineage but has מצוות. A גוי has lineage but no מצוות. That is why both needed their own exclusion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכותא: the גמרא proves that two seemingly overlapping rules are each needed.

phrases.english: And it is necessary [to state both];
for if it had taught us only a slave,
[I would say he is excluded] because he has no lineage,
but a gentile, who does have lineage,
I might say no [he is not excluded];
and if it had taught us only a gentile,
[I would say he is excluded] because he has no connection to מצוות,
but a slave, who is connected to מצוות,
I might say no;
[therefore] it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why step 1 needed two separate exclusions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the עבד nor the גוי can be learned from the other, so both exclusions are needed.

steps.title: Where do we learn that women are included in damages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's statement that women are included in the laws of damage and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And women are included in the laws of damage. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says women are treated like men in נזיקין. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this, rather than just accepting it.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in the laws of damage

phrases.english: And women are included in [the laws of] damage.
From where are these words [derived]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of witnesses and turns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that women are equal to men in the laws of damages.

steps.title: A woman is equal to a man for all Torah punishments
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב, together with the school of רבי ישמעאל, cites 'איש או אשה' (במדבר 5:6) to show that the Torah treats women like men for all punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: The verse says, 'A man or a woman who commits any sin.' The verse made a woman equal to a man for all the punishments in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that mentions both man and woman together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק says 'איש או אשה', it is read as a general rule: women and men are equal for all עונשין in the Torah. This includes paying for damages, so women are included in נזיקין.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

steps.whatToRemember: 'איש או אשה' teaches that women and men are equal for all Torah punishments, including damages.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught the same:
The verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַעֲשׂוּ מִכׇּל חַטֹּאת״ –
phrases.english: "A man or a woman who commits any of the sins":
the verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the punishments in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'איש או אשה' makes women equal to men for all Torah punishments, including damages.

steps.title: Second source: women and men are equal in all civil laws
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אלעזר learns from 'ואלה המשפטים אשר תשים לפניהם' that the Torah treats women like men in all civil laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אלעזר taught: 'And these are the laws that you shall set before them.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all the civil laws in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the question of where we learn that women are included in the laws of damage. This one comes from the school of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step 4 source was about punishments. This source is about דינין, the civil and money laws, like lawsuits and payments. 'Before them' means before all the people, men and women alike.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of (a Sage's study hall)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Elazar taught:
"And these are the laws
that you shall set before them" —
phrases.notes: שמות 21:1. 'Them' means the whole nation, women too.

phrases.english: the verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the civil laws in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the question in step 3, in addition to the source in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ואלה המשפטים אשר תשים לפניהם teaches that women equal men for all civil laws.

steps.title: Third source: a woman's death is treated like a man's
steps.stepSummary: The school of חזקיה and רבי יוסי הגלילי learn from 'והמית איש או אשה' that the Torah treats a woman like a man for all deaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of חזקיה and רבי יוסי הגלילי taught: the verse says, 'and it killed a man or a woman.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all killings in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source. It comes from the פסוק about an ox that kills a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source is about the victim, not the one who caused the damage. If an ox kills a woman, the owner's liability is the same as if it killed a man.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי תָּנָא,
phrases.english: The school of Chizkiya and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili taught:
The verse says: "and it killed a man or a woman" —
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29. It's talking about an ox that kills a person.

phrases.english: the verse made a woman equal to a man
for all the killings in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third source next to the sources in steps 4 and 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: והמית איש או אשה teaches that a woman equals a man for all killings.

steps.title: Why the atonement source alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all the sources are needed. From the first source (punishment and atonement) alone, we might think women are not included in civil law, because women usually were not in business.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are needed. If the Torah taught us only the first source, I would say: there the Torah had pity on her so that she could get atonement. But in civil laws, a man, who does business, yes, is included. A woman, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why we need more than one source (a צריכותא). First it shows that the 'punishment' source from step 4 could not teach us civil law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step 4 source includes women in punishments for a good reason: paying brings her כפרה, and the Torah wants that for her. That reason has nothing to do with business. Since women were usually not involved in business, we might have left them out of the civil laws. So the source in step 5 is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they are needed (all the sources are necessary)

phrases.english: And they are needed;
for if it had taught us only the first one —
phrases.notes: The 'first one' is 'איש או אשה' from step 4, about punishments.

phrases.english: I would say that there, the Merciful One had pity on her,
so that she could have atonement;
but in civil laws —
a man, who does business — yes,
a woman — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing several sources, the גמרא explains why each one is necessary, starting with the source from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment source has its own reason (atonement), so it cannot teach that women are included in civil law.

steps.title: Why the civil-law source alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: From the civil-law source alone, we might think women are included only so they can earn a living. We might also think they do not need atonement, since they are not obligated in all מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah taught us only civil laws, I would say that is so she can make a living. But atonement: a man, who is obligated in מצוות, yes. A woman, who is not obligated in מצוות, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכותא in the other direction. It shows that the civil-law source from step 5 could not teach us the punishment and atonement law from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are included in civil law for a practical reason: if the laws did not apply to her, people would not do business with her, and she could not support herself. That reason does not apply to כפרה. Since a woman is not obligated in all the מצוות like a man, we might think she does not need atonement. So the source in step 4 is needed too.

keyTerms.meaning: Livelihood, a way to support oneself
One who is obligated in מצוות (for a woman: בַּת מִצְוָה)

steps.whatToRemember: The punishment source and the civil-law source each have their own reason, so neither can be learned from the other. Each one is needed.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only civil laws —
I would say that is so she can make a living;
phrases.notes: If the civil laws did not apply to her, people would be afraid to do business with her.

phrases.english: but atonement —
a man, who is obligated in מצוות — yes;
a woman, who is not obligated in מצוות — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second direction of the צריכותא begun in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The civil-law source has its own reason (livelihood), so it cannot teach that women need atonement through punishment.

steps.title: The first two sources would not teach the case of killing
steps.stepSummary: Even with both the atonement source and the civil-law source, we could not learn that the owner pays כופר when his ox kills a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had taught only these two sources, we would say: here she is included because she needs atonement, and there because she needs to make a living. But for killing, we would say that only for a man, who is obligated in מצוות, the owner pays כופר; for a woman, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of reasons why every source is needed. Now it shows that even the first two sources together would not cover the third case: an ox that kills a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the first two sources has its own special reason for including women: כפרה and earning a living. Neither reason applies to כופר. Since a man is a בר מצוה, obligated in all מצוות, we might have thought his life alone counts for כופר. That is why the third source, 'והמית איש או אשה', is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom the owner pays when his ox kills a person

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only these two
phrases.notes: These are the first two sources: punishment and atonement (step 4), and civil law (step 5).

phrases.english: here it is because of atonement,
and here it is because of making a living;
but regarding killing,
for a man, who is obligated in מצוות,
the owner must pay ransom;
for a woman, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from steps 7-8, now showing that the third source cannot be learned from the first two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first two sources have their own special reasons, כפרה and earning a living, so they could not teach that כופר is paid for a woman.

steps.title: The killing source alone would not teach the other two, so all are needed
steps.stepSummary: From the כופר source alone we could not learn the first two cases, so the גמרא concludes that all three sources are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had taught only about כופר, we would say that is because a life was lost. But in those two cases, where no life is lost, we would say women are not included. Therefore all the sources are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the last direction: the כופר source could not teach the other two. It then closes the discussion with 'צריכא', meaning all three sources are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing a life is very serious, so we might have thought the Torah includes a woman only there. The other two cases do not involve איבוד נשמה, so we might have left women out. This completes the proof that none of the three פסוקים is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; each source is necessary

steps.whatToRemember: Women and men are equal in punishments and atonement, in civil laws, and in כופר. Each needs its own פסוק because each case has a special reason that would not carry over to the others.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only ransom,
that would be because a life was lost;
but these two,
where no life is lost,
I would say no, women are not included;
therefore it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא by showing the third source cannot teach the first two, then concludes 'צריכא'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three פסוקים are needed. Each one teaches equality between women and men in an area the others could not cover.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה: the injured party and the damager share the payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The injured party and the one who caused the damage are both involved in the payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next words. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's phrase suggests that in some cases both the ניזק and the מזיק carry part of the loss. The גמרא quotes it here to open a new topic about the half-damage payment, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The injured party, the one who suffered damage
The one responsible for the damage

phrases.english: The injured party and the one liable for the damage are both involved in the payment.
phrases.notes: These are words from the משנה that the גמרא is now going to discuss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the topic of women and men, the גמרא moves on to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה states that both the injured party and the damager take part in the payment.

steps.title: Is half-damage regular payment or a fine?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the half-damage payment is ממונא, regular compensation. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says it is קנסא, a fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: about half-damage, רב פפא says it is regular compensation, and רב הונא the son of רב יהושע says it is a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement between two אמוראים about the nature of פלגא נזקא, the half payment for damage by an ox that is not yet known to gore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is ממונא, the payment is ordinary compensation for the loss. If it is קנסא, it is a penalty the Torah imposes, not a simple repayment of a debt. This is connected to the משנה's phrase that both the ניזק and the מזיק carry part of the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of the damage, the payment for a תם ox
Regular monetary compensation for a loss
A fine, a penalty set by the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the amount: half the damage is paid. They disagree only about what kind of payment it is, regular compensation or a fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: Calling a payment ממון or קנס can change how the law treats it, so this מחלוקת sets up the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: It was said: half-damage,
phrases.notes: This is the half payment for damage by an ox that hasn't yet been established as a gorer.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: it is monetary compensation,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: קְנָסָא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, says: it is a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's phrase about both parties sharing the payment by asking what kind of payment half-damage is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא holds that פלגא נזקא is ממונא. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds that it is קנסא.

steps.title: Why רב פפא calls half-damage real compensation
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא holds that ordinary oxen are not assumed to be safe. So the owner should really pay full damage, but the Torah went easy on him because his ox had not yet been warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says the half payment is regular compensation. He holds that ordinary oxen are not assumed to be safe, so the owner should really pay for all the damage. The Torah had pity on him and cut it to half, because his ox was never warned before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב פפא's view that half-damage is ממונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since oxen are not assumed to be safe, the owner had a duty to guard his ox, and full payment would be fair. Paying only half is a break the Torah gives him, because a תם ox never showed it gores. So the half he pays is real money he truly owes.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary oxen, ones with no record of goring
A presumption of being safe, meaning not likely to cause harm
The Merciful One, a name for God or the Torah
Was warned, meaning it became a מועד

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: it is monetary compensation
He holds: ordinary oxen
are not presumed to be safe,
so by right he should have to pay all of it;
but it is the Merciful One who had pity on him,
since his ox has not yet been warned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב פפא's position stated in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary oxen are not presumed safe, so full payment would be fair; the half is a reduction the Torah granted, and what is paid is real compensation.

steps.title: Why רב הונא calls half-damage a fine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע holds that ordinary oxen are assumed to be safe. So the owner should really pay nothing, but the Torah fined him so he would guard his ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע says the half payment is a fine. He holds that ordinary oxen are assumed to be safe, so the owner should really pay nothing. The Torah fined him anyway, so that he would guard his ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the opposite view: half-damage is a קנס, a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the starting point flips. If oxen are normally safe, the owner did nothing wrong by not guarding it and would owe nothing. The Torah adds a payment as a penalty to push owners to be careful, so the money is not something the injured party truly deserves.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine or penalty, not payment of a real debt

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the owner pays half. They argue only about what kind of payment it is. This matters later for rules that apply to fines but not to compensation.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר קְנָסָא –
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua says: it is a fine
He holds: ordinary oxen
are presumed to be safe,
so by right he should not pay at all;
but it is the Merciful One who fined him,
so that he will guard his ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר קְנָסָא – קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reasoning, set side by side with רב פפא's in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary oxen are presumed safe, so by right nothing would be owed; the half payment is a penalty meant to make owners guard their oxen.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument rests on one assumption: are oxen normally safe or not? That assumption decides whether the half payment is a debt or a penalty.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: how does the injured party share in paying?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the injured party and the damager both share in the payment. That fits ממונא, because the victim loses half of what he deserves. Under קנסא the victim deserves nothing, so how does he share in paying?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'The injured party and the damager share in the payment.' That works for the one who says half-damage is compensation, because the victim gives up half of what is really his. But for the one who says it is a fine, the victim is getting money that isn't really his. How can you say he shares in the payment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the wording of the משנה to challenge רב הונא's view that half-damage is a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ממונא, the victim truly deserves full payment and gets only half, so he 'pays' by losing the other half. Under קנסא, he deserves nothing, and any money he gets is a bonus. So he does not seem to lose anything, and the משנה's words seem not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The one responsible for the damage
Half the damage, the payment for a תם ox

phrases.english: We learned: the injured party and the damager are in the payment.
Granted, according to the one who says
half-damage is compensation
that is why the injured party is part of the payment;
but according to the one who says
half-damage is a fine
now that what he takes is not even his,
is he part of the payment?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from steps 13 and 14 against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's view that half-damage is קנסא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the victim deserves nothing by right, he loses nothing. Then the משנה's statement that he shares in the payment has no meaning.

steps.title: Answer: the injured party absorbs the drop in the carcass's value
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's phrase refers to פחת נבילה. The injured party bears the loss as the dead animal's value goes down, and that is how he shares in the payment, even under קנסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's phrase is needed only for the loss in value of the carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the קנסא view. It explains that 'the injured party shares in the payment' means something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not mean the victim gives up half of what he deserves. It means that if the dead animal loses value before the court case, that loss falls on the victim. So he shares in the loss in a real way, and the משנה fits the קנסא view too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for, meaning the phrase refers to a specific point
The drop in value of the dead animal's carcass

steps.whatToRemember: ממונא means oxen are not presumed safe and the half is a reduction. קנסא means oxen are presumed safe and the half is a penalty. The משנה's 'the injured party shares in the payment' fits even קנסא, because the victim bears פחת נבילה.

phrases.english: It is needed only
for the drop in value of the carcass.
phrases.notes: The dead animal loses value over time, and that loss falls on the owner of the dead animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by reading the משנה's phrase differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה's phrase to refer to a different loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase means the victim gives up half of what he deserves, which fits only ממונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means the victim bears the drop in the carcass's value, which fits קנסא as well.

steps.title: The carcass loss was already taught earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 16. The idea that the victim bears the loss of the carcass's value was already taught in the first part of the משנה, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The diminishing value of the carcass? But the first clause already taught that: 'Payments for damage' teaches that the owners deal with the carcass!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the phrase about sharing means פחת נבילה, the משנה would be saying the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא learned from the words תשלומי נזק that the injured party keeps the dead animal, so he takes any drop in its value. If the later phrase also means פחת נבילה, it adds nothing new. A משנה does not normally repeat itself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The drop in value of the dead animal
The first clause or opening part of a teaching
Deal with the carcass; they keep it and take its loss

phrases.english: The diminishing value of the carcass?
But it already taught it in the first clause:
'Payments for damage'
teaches that the owners deal with the carcass!
phrases.notes: The גמרא learned this from the משנה's wording back on 10b. 'The owners' are the owners of the injured animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16 by saying it makes the משנה repeat itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's phrase about sharing in payment means פחת נבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: the first clause already taught that the victim bears the carcass loss, so reading the later phrase the same way makes it pointless.

steps.title: One mention is for a תם, one for a מועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches פחת נבילה twice because one mention is about a תם and the other is about a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about an innocuous ox, and one is about a forewarned ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two mentions are not a repeat, because each one covers a different kind of ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the victim bears the carcass loss applies both to a תם and to a מועד. The משנה states it once for each. The next step explains why one mention would not have been enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox not yet warned; it has not gored three times
A forewarned ox, known to gore; its owner pays full damage

phrases.english: One is about an innocuous ox, and one is about a forewarned ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each mention covers a different type of ox.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both mentions teach the exact same thing, so one is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One mention covers a תם and the other covers a מועד, so neither is extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the answer of step 16, so the קנסא view can still explain the משנה.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why we could not learn the מועד from the תם, or the תם from the מועד. Each case has its own reason to go easy on the owner, so both must be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary. If it had taught only a תם, I would say the owner is let off because his ox was not yet warned, but a מועד is not. If it had taught only a מועד, I would say he is let off because he already pays the full damage, but a תם is not. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing that each mention teaches something we could not have guessed from the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a תם, the owner gets a break because his ox had no warning, a reason that does not apply to a מועד. For a מועד, the owner gets a break because he is already paying full damage, a reason that does not apply to a תם. Since each reason fits only one case, the משנה had to state both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; both cases need to be stated

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה states פחת נבילה twice, once for a תם and once for a מועד, and each is needed. So the קנסא view can still read the phrase about sharing as פחת נבילה.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught us only an innocuous ox,
I would say that is because it was not yet warned,
phrases.notes: Read it as 'I would say the owner is let off because...', which is why the owner doesn't bear the carcass loss.

phrases.english: but with a forewarned ox, I would say not.
And if it had taught us only a forewarned ox,
I would say that is because he pays all of it,
but with an innocuous ox, I would say not;
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of step 18 by showing that neither case could be learned from the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that both cases are needed: each case has a reason that does not carry over to the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could learn one case from the other, so stating both is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has its own reason for going easy on the owner, so both had to be stated.

steps.title: A new proof from the difference between תם and מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a תם pays half damage only from its own body, while a מועד pays full damage from the owner's best property. This sets up a new attempt to decide between ממונא and קנסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: What is the difference between a תם and a מועד? A תם pays half damage only from its own body, and a מועד pays full damage from the owner's best property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof by quoting a משנה about how a תם and a מועד pay. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try to use this משנה to decide between ממונא and קנסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a תם, the victim can only collect from the body of the goring ox. If it is worth too little, he loses out. With a מועד, the owner must pay in full from his best land. The גמרא will now ask which view, ממונא or קנסא, fits this limit on a תם's payment.

keyTerms.meaning: From its body; payment comes only from the goring ox itself
From the best-quality property of the owner

phrases.english: Come and hear:
What is the difference between an innocuous ox and a forewarned ox?
phrases.notes: This is a משנה that comes later, on 16b.

phrases.english: The innocuous one pays half damage, from its own body,
phrases.notes: The victim can collect only up to the value of the goring ox itself, and nothing from the owner's other things.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוּעָד מְשַׁלֵּם נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם – מִן הָעֲלִיָּיה.
phrases.english: and the forewarned one pays full damage, from the best property.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מָה בֵּין תָּם לְמוּעָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the קנסא view, the גמרא leaves that line and brings a new source to test the debate of steps 12-14.
steps.raayaObject: The debate between רב פפא (ממונא) and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע (קנסא) about half damage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 16b listing the payment differences between a תם and a מועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: The limit that a תם pays only from its body is a key rule. The גמרא will test whether it fits better with ממונא or קנסא.

steps.title: Why doesn't the list include paying by admission?
steps.stepSummary: If a תם's payment is קנסא, the משנה should also have listed that a תם's owner does not pay by his own admission, while a מועד's owner does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is true that a תם's payment is a fine, the משנה should also teach this difference: the owner of a תם does not pay if he admits it himself, but the owner of a מועד does pay if he admits it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה's list of differences between a תם and a מועד to push against the קנסא view. If קנסא were true, one more difference should be on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a person who admits on his own to something that carries a fine does not pay it (מודה בקנס פטור). So if a תם's half-damage is קנסא, admitting does not obligate him, while a מועד's full payment is ממונא and admitting does. That is a clear difference, and the משנה does not mention it, which suggests the payment is ממונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if the claim is true)
Let it teach (the משנה should have said)
Based on his own word (his own admission)
One who admits to a fine is exempt from paying it

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a תם's half-damage payment really is a fine (קנסא).

phrases.english: let it also teach this:

phrases.aramaic: תָּם אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: an innocuous ox's owner does not pay based on his own admission,
a forewarned ox's owner pays based on his own admission!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה brought in step 20 and draws a challenge to the קנסא view from what the משנה leaves out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a תם's half-damage payment is קנסא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were קנסא, the difference about paying by admission would exist and should have been listed. Since it is not listed, it seems the payment is ממונא.

steps.title: The תנא taught some cases and left some out
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is not a complete list. The תנא taught some differences and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught, and he left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the קנסא view by saying the משנה's list is not complete. The admission difference was simply left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument from silence only works if the list is complete. By saying 'תנא ושייר', the גמרא removes the proof: leaving the admission difference out does not show it doesn't exist.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught and left out; the list is not complete

phrases.english: He taught and left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists every difference between a תם and a מועד, so a missing difference does not exist.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left some differences out, so the admission difference can be real even though it is not listed.

steps.title: What else was left out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the תנא left this out, what other case did he also leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that you can say he left this out too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 22. It wants to know what else is missing from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא's working rule is that 'תנא ושייר' only works if at least one more item is missing. A list that is missing just one item would look like that item doesn't exist. So the answer must point to a second missing case.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a simple request for information. The גמרא is testing whether 'תנא ושייר' can really be said here, since it needs a second missing item.

phrases.english: What else did he leave out, that he left out this?
phrases.notes: A תנא doesn't leave out just one thing. Show me another missing case, and then we can accept that this one is missing too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'תנא ושייר' needs at least one more missing case. Without one, the answer does not hold.

steps.title: Half ransom was also left out
steps.stepSummary: The second missing item is חצי כופר: a תם that kills a person does not pay even half ransom, while a מועד pays full ransom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out half ransom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names another difference the משנה did not list, the law of כופר (ransom) when an ox kills a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a מועד ox kills a person, its owner pays כופר. When a תם kills, the owner pays no כופר at all, not even half. That is a real difference between תם and מועד that the משנה did not mention, so there is a second missing item.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom payment when an ox kills a person

phrases.english: He left out half ransom.
phrases.notes: He means: a תם that kills a person does not pay even half the ransom, while a מועד pays the full ransom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand of step 23 by naming a second missing item.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing else is missing from the list, so 'תנא ושייר' fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference about חצי כופר is also missing, so the list really is incomplete.

steps.title: Half ransom is not missing according to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects step 24. The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that a תם does pay חצי כופר, so nothing about כופר was left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was because of half ransom, that is not something left out. Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says a תם pays half ransom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second missing item. Without it, 'תנא ושייר' fails, and the challenge from step 21 is open again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that a תם that kills pays חצי כופר, the same way it pays half damages. Under his view, the משנה's rule that a תם pays half already covers כופר, so nothing is missing. The admission difference is again the only missing item, which points back toward ממונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Something left out of a list

steps.whyThisMatters: Once the only other missing item is gone, the question 'why doesn't the משנה list admission?' returns. That pressure on the קנסא view carries into the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: If it is because of half ransom,
that is not something left out;
whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who says: an innocuous ox pays half ransom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם חֲצִי כוֹפֶר – לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24. That brings back the challenge of step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חצי כופר as a second missing item, so the 'תנא ושייר' defense from step 22 has nothing to stand on.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 24 assumed a תם pays no כופר at all. The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds a תם pays חצי כופר, so that difference is already included in 'a תם pays half'.

steps.title: Come and hear: a new proof is introduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it is about to bring a new source as a proof in the ongoing question about a תם's payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says 'come and hear,' which tells us a source is about to be quoted as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 21-25 it was the defense of the קנסא view that fell, not the challenge. Step 25 removed the 'תנא ושייר' answer, so the challenge from step 21 still stands. The גמרא now opens a fresh attempt with a new source, and the proof itself comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: This line has no content of its own. Don't look for the proof here; it is only the doorway to the source quoted next.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 rejected the חצי כופר suggestion, the גמרא turns to a new source to try again.
steps.raayaObject: The open question of whether a תם's payment is ממונא or קנסא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about to be quoted (from כתובות)
